title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement
requirement: After a tenant has occupied a property for 12 months, the owner must have just cause to terminate the tenancy and must state that cause in the written notice.
coverage_conditions: residential real property where all tenants have occupied for 12 months or at least one tenant has occupied for 24 months
exemptions: transient hotels, nonprofit hospitals/religious facilities, dormitories, owner-occupied units with shared facilities, single-family owner-occupied residences, two-unit properties where owner occupies one, housing built within the last 15 years, certain alienable single-family homes, deed-restricted affordable housing
quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Eviction
requirement: If an owner terminates a tenancy for a no-fault just cause, they must provide relocation assistance equal to one month's rent or waive the final month's rent.
coverage_conditions: residential real property subject to just cause requirements
exemptions: transient hotels, nonprofit hospitals/religious facilities, dormitories, owner-occupied units with shared facilities, single-family owner-occupied residences, two-unit properties where owner occupies one, housing built within the last 15 years, certain alienable single-family homes, deed-restricted affordable housing
quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month's rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.

title: Section 1946.2 of the Civil Code
requirement: After a tenant has occupied a property for 12 months (or 24 months if only one tenant has occupied it), a landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy.
exemptions: mobilehome homeowners as defined in Section 798.9
overrides: local ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019
local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 that are more protective
interaction: preemption; local ordinances that are more protective apply instead of this section
quoted_span: California law also provides that after all of the tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more or at least one of the tenants has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 24 months or more, a landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy.
